newsitem.title: UK: C&W up, HK Telecom stake sale clears overhang.
newsitem.headline: C&W up, HK Telecom stake sale clears overhang.

text.p: Shares in Cable and Wireless Plc rose on Friday, after CITIC Pacific agreed to its remaining 7.74 percent stake in Hongkong Telecom, to China Everbright, removing a stock overhang which had depressed HK Telecom's share price.
C&W, which has a 58.5 percent stake in Hongkong Telecom, put on 13-1/2p to 515p, having hit 520p.
"CITIC has been a seller of the shares. They had been flogging the shares in the market and whittling down their holding but this has removed the overhang," said one telecoms analyst.
Hongkong Telecom shares have risen sharply this week and on Thursday the company revealed 12.5 percent growth in its net profits this year.
The price being paid by China Everbright is below Thursday's market price but above that of Hongkong Telecom shares earlier this week, analysts said.
"It's clearly not the price paid which has pushed Cable shares higher - it's the removal of the stock hanging over the market," said another analyst.
"Now we have to find out which Chinese state enterprise or department China Everbright is linked to," he said.

CITIC is a hybrid - Chinese state-owned but listed, with private shareholders, analysts said. China Everbright is state-owned but analysts said were not clear on whether the company was linked to China United Telecommunications Corp (China Unicom) or China's Ministry of Post and Telecommunications.
C&W said it welcomed the planned Chinese state investment in Hongkong Telecom.

"This substantial investment of Chinese state capital demonstrates continued confidence in Hongkong Telecom and Hong Kong through the 1997 transition and beyond," said the chairman of Cable and Wireless Group and Hongkong Telecom.
